The lesson explains how a truth table assigns a full-statement value to every possible input case, then demonstrates all four pairs for conjunction.

Negation, conjunction, inclusive disjunction, and material implication each have operational truth conditions, not merely names. The combined example shows how to substitute an inner result before evaluating the outer connective.
Inclusive or explicitly includes both-true inputs and excludes only both-false inputs. Conjunction explicitly fails if either input is false.
The conditional includes the easily missed false-if-part case, regardless of Q. Shortcut applicability is limited to the statements joined by that connective, with inner parentheses evaluated first.
